claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, he's over 16, so I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This includes full-time, non-advanced education such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar qualifications, but does not include university or other higher education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and hasn't started anything new yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex has left education, there may still be a way for you to qualify for Child Benefit for a limited period.

**Has Alex registered with any of the following since leaving education?**

1. A government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service in England, Careers Wales, Skills Development Scotland, or similar)
2. The armed services

If he has registered with either of these within the last 20 weeks, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with any careers service or the armed forces. He just left school and that's it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying.

I have one more important question to check eligibility:

**Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all, and he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just a couple more questions about your circumstances:

**Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all of that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- Alex is 17 years old
- He has left education and is not in any approved education or training
- He has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- He is not working 24+ hours per week and does not receive benefits in his own right
- You live in the UK and Alex lives with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Unfortunately, I have to share some news that may not be what you were hoping for.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why?

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit normally only continues if the child remains in **approved education or training**. There is an exception that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services

Since Alex is 17, has left education, is not currently in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, he does not meet the criteria for Child Benefit.

### What could change this?

If Alex were to:
1. **Enrol in approved education or training** (such as A-levels, a BTEC, or an NVQ up to level 3), or
2. **Register with a government-sponsored careers service** (you may be able to claim for up to 20 weeks if this happens soon after leaving education)

...you may then become eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

I hope this information is helpful. If Alex's circumstances change or if you have any other questions, please don't hesitate to ask.
